title: Koszul substitution with determinant invertible modulo the generated ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\geq0$, and $a,b:\{1,\ldots,r\}\to A$ such that $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$. Put $E=A^{\oplus r}$ with standard basis $e_i$, and let $\alpha,\beta:E\to A$ be the linear maps $\alpha(e_i)=a_i$, $\beta(e_i)=b_i$. Let $t:E\to E$ be an $A$-linear map satisfying $\alpha\circ t=\beta$. Let $\delta$ be the determinant of its matrix in the standard basis. Suppose that the class of $\delta$ is a unit in $A/I$. For the Koszul complexes [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], the exterior-power maps $\bigwedge^q t$ form a chain map $T:K_\bullet(A,b)\to K_\bullet(A,a)$. This map is a quasi-isomorphism; equivalently, after placing homological degree $q$ in cochain degree $-q$, the specified morphism $Q(T):Q(K_\bullet(A,b))\to Q(K_\bullet(A,a))$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No regularity, proper-ideal, Noetherian, or local hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 066A (lemma-independence-of-generators), proof, second paragraph: the matrix-induced Koszul comparison is an isomorphism after inverting its determinant, and the homology is annihilated by the common ideal.

proof.text: Write $K_b=K_\bullet(A,b)$ and $K_a=K_\bullet(A,a)$. The tensor map induced by $t$ preserves the ideal generated by $v\otimes v$, since it sends that generator to $t(v)\otimes t(v)$; it therefore induces $T_q=\bigwedge^q t$, sending $v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_q$ to $t(v_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge t(v_q)$. On such a wedge the contraction formula gives $d_aT_q=T_{q-1}d_b$: the coefficient in the $i$th summand on the left is $\alpha(t(v_i))=\beta(v_i)$ and the omitted wedge is the image under $T_{q-1}$ of the omitted source wedge. These wedges span, so the equality holds everywhere. In degree zero both maps are the identity of $A$ and the outgoing differential is zero. This constructs the specified chain map with its stated direction.

source.place: Tag 0624, lemma-functorial; Tag 0622, definition-koszul and the displayed contraction formula

proof.text: For either tuple $f=a$ or $f=b$, the cited generator homotopy says $f_i\operatorname{id}=dh_i+h_id$, with $h_i(x)=e_i\wedge x$. If $z$ is a cycle then $f_i z=d(h_i z)$, so $f_i[z]=0$. Every element of $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is a finite $A$-linear combination of these generators, hence annihilates every $H_q(K_f)$. The two generated ideals are both $I$, so $I H_q(K_a)=I H_q(K_b)=0$ for every $q$. For the empty tuple this merely asserts annihilation by the zero ideal.

source.place: Tag 0663, lemma-homotopy-koszul, deduced from Tag 0626, lemma-homotopy-koszul-abstract

proof.text: Put $S=\{\delta^n:n\geq0\}$ and $B=S^{-1}A$. Localize the complexes termwise. The increasing standard wedges give a basis of each exterior power; sending each localized standard wedge to the same standard wedge over $B$ identifies $S^{-1}K_f$ with $K_\bullet(B,f/1)$. The differential agrees under this identification because its contraction formula has coefficients $f_i/1$, and the localized $T$ sends a wedge to the wedge of the images under the matrix $M/1$ of $t$. The adjugate identity gives the two-sided inverse $(\delta/1)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(M/1)$ to $M/1$. Applying its exterior powers gives two-sided inverses in every degree: the composites fix each decomposable wedge. Thus $S^{-1}T$ is an isomorphism of complexes (its degreewise inverse commutes with the differential by multiplying the chain equation by the two inverses). This also covers $q>r$, where both terms vanish, and $r=0$, where the degree-zero map is the identity.

source.place: Tag 066A, lemma-independence-of-generators, proof second paragraph; Tags 00DM and 07DQ for the standard wedge basis and adjugate identity

proof.text: For either $K=K_a$ or $K_b$, write $Z_q=\ker d_q$ and $B_q=\operatorname{im}d_{q+1}$, with $B_{-1}=0$. Apply exactness of module localization to $0\to Z_q\to K_q\to B_{q-1}\to0$ and $0\to B_q\to Z_q\to H_q(K)\to0$. The localized inclusion $B_{q-1}\to K_{q-1}$ remains injective, so the first sequence identifies the cycles of the localized complex with $S^{-1}Z_q$; the localized surjection $K_{q+1}\to B_q$ identifies its boundaries with $S^{-1}B_q$. The second sequence then identifies its homology with $S^{-1}H_q(K)$. These identifications send $[z]/\delta^n$ to $[z/\delta^n]$, and are natural for $T$, since both orders send this element to $[Tz/\delta^n]$. Consequently $S^{-1}H_q(T)$ is bijective, by the complex isomorphism in Step 3.

source.place: Tag 066A, lemma-independence-of-generators, proof second paragraph; Tag 00HT, lemma-flat-localization, proof recalling exact localization

proof.text: Choose $c\in A$ lifting the inverse of $\overline\delta$ in $A/I$, so $c\delta-1\in I$. On each homology module $N=H_q(K_a)$ or $H_q(K_b)$, Step 2 gives $c\delta=1$ as scalar endomorphisms. The canonical map $\lambda_N:N\to S^{-1}N$ is therefore bijective, with inverse $x/\delta^n\mapsto c^n x$. Indeed, if $\delta^k(\delta^m x-\delta^n y)=0$, multiplying by $c^{k+n+m}$ gives $c^n x=c^m y$, proving this formula well-defined; its two composites with $\lambda_N$ are identities. Naturality is the equality $H_q(T)(c^n x)=c^n H_q(T)(x)$. Hence $H_q(T)=\lambda_{H_q(K_a)}^{-1}\circ S^{-1}H_q(T)\circ\lambda_{H_q(K_b)}$ is bijective for every $q$. No assumption that $\delta$ is a unit in $A$ was used.

source.place: Tag 066A, lemma-independence-of-generators, proof second paragraph, spelling out why localization does not change the two homology modules

proof.text: The homology isomorphisms just proved say that the specified $T$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Placing degree $q$ in cochain degree $-q$ leaves these same homology maps in degrees $-q$ and has zero cohomology in positive degrees. The derived localization $Q$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms, so this very $Q(T)$ is an isomorphism. Conversely, if $Q(T)$ is invertible, apply each cohomology functor, which factors through $Q$, to recover these same homology isomorphisms. This proves the stated equivalence.

lean.statement: theorem koszul_substitution_unit_mod_ideal (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} A)] (r : ℕ) (a b : Fin r → A) (I : Ideal A) (ha : Ideal.span (Set.range a) = I) (hb : Ideal.span (Set.range b) = I) (t : (Fin r →₀ A) →ₗ[A] (Fin r →₀ A)) (ht : (Finsupp.linearCombination A a).comp t = Finsupp.linearCombination A b) (hδ : IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (Matrix.det (fun i j : Fin r ↦ t (Finsupp.single j 1) i)))) : ∃ T : koszulComplex A r b ⟶ koszulComplex A r a, (∀ q : ℕ, (T.f q).hom = exteriorPower.map q t) ∧ QuasiIso T ∧ IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map (HomologicalComplex.extendMap T ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat))

reviewed_lean.note: Statement matches node and Stacks 066A (proof, 2nd paragraph) / 0624 clause by clause. A comm ring at universe u with no extra instances. Explicit I with span(a)=I and span(b)=I. E=Fin r→₀A with α,β the linearCombination maps, the same φ as ExteriorAlgebra.koszulComplex. ht: α∘t=β. det of (t e_j)_i is a unit in A⧸I, not in A. ∃T : K(b)⟶K(a) with every component (T.f q).hom = exteriorPower.map q t, so T is unique and points the 0624 way. Concludes QuasiIso T and IsIso (Q.map (extendMap T embeddingDownNat)), so the derived-category form is present. HasDerivedCategory.{w} is the size convention only. Edge cases: r=0, A=0, I=A, I=0, ℤ with det 3 mod 2, q>r. No duplicate in Mathlib or side-live (only a private generatorMap_exists helper with the same convention).
